ecological_question: Are species that are more strongly recruited into wetter active assemblages characterized by shorter, more concentrated breeding seasons?

response_source.response: pair-covariate-adjusted per-species wet-versus-dry intercept log odds

trait_source.source_definition: Description from contributing natural-history references of the times of year when a species breeds; ATraiU also stores month modalities.

computational_transport.provenance: Species-level text carried from the ATraiU reference-level database by deterministic mode_nonnull collapse in the transport repository. Scientific attribution remains ATraiU.

taxonomy.normalization: first two binomial tokens after whitespace trim
match_order: frozen genus alias only if exact fails

frozen_parser.range_rule: MonthA followed by '-', 'to', or 'through' and MonthB expands inclusively; ranges crossing December wrap through January.
frozen_parser.union_rule: Final breeding-season months are the union of expanded month ranges, standalone month tokens, mapped season words, or all 12 months for year-round phrases.
frozen_parser.missing_rule: If no month, season word, or year-round phrase is recognized, breadth is missing.
frozen_parser.output: breeding_season_breadth_months = number of unique recognized months, range 1-12.

primary_model.estimator: inverse-variance weighted least squares with HC3 covariance across species
primary_model.hypothesis: Shorter breeding seasons predict more positive wet-recruitment responses.

family_structure_sensitivity.method: weighted within-family slope after subtracting weighted family means from breeding-season breadth and adjusted response
family_structure_sensitivity.permutation: permute breeding-season breadth among species within family
family_structure_sensitivity.inference: two-sided Monte Carlo P plus negative-tail P

descriptive_groups.status: descriptive only; no threshold-based confirmatory test

boundaries: This is a post-opening mechanistic follow-up, not an original preregistered hypothesis.
ATraiU breeding-season text may summarize geographically variable literature and is not a local NAAMP phenology measurement.
Breeding-season breadth is a proxy for temporal reproductive strategy and is not identical to the classical explosive/prolonged classification.
A supported relationship would motivate a pulse-tracking breeding-strategy interpretation but would not establish rainfall causality or reproductive success.
No additional ATraiU traits may be promoted within this analysis family after readback.
